problemText: Which statement correctly describes the difference between a topic and a central idea?
choices: A topic is a word or short phrase that names what a text is about, while a central idea is a complete sentence that states the main point the text makes about that topic.
A topic is a complete sentence that expresses the full main idea, while a central idea is just a single word or short phrase that identifies the subject being discussed.
A topic and a central idea are two names for the same concept and serve identical purposes when analyzing any piece of writing or text.
A topic is something mentioned only in titles or introductions, while a central idea is a detail that must appear in the body paragraphs to support the topic.
hints: Remember the lesson: a topic is very short, while a central idea must be a full sentence.
Think about 'earthworms' versus 'Earthworms make soil healthier in more than one way.' Which is the topic and which is the central idea?

problemText: Read this paragraph: 'Monarch butterflies migrate thousands of miles each year to escape cold winters. They travel south in enormous groups, sometimes numbering in the millions. Scientists track these migrations using special tags attached to the butterflies' wings. The journey takes several months, and the butterflies rest on milkweed plants along the way.' Which statement is the central idea of this paragraph?
choices: Monarch butterflies are tagged by scientists using special equipment attached to their wings for research purposes.
Monarch butterflies migrate thousands of miles each year in massive groups to survive cold winters, a journey that takes several months.
Monarch butterflies need to rest frequently on milkweed plants during their annual journey because the migration is physically demanding and exhausting.
Scientists have developed methods to study monarch butterfly migrations by attaching tracking devices to individual butterflies in the population.
hints: The central idea should cover what the paragraph keeps returning to across every sentence, not just one fact from one sentence.
Look for a sentence that includes the reason (why) the butterflies migrate, how many travel together, and how long it takes—the main points the paragraph adds up to.

problemText: Read this passage: 'Coral reefs are made up of tiny animals called polyps that build hard outer skeletons. These skeletons stack on top of each other over hundreds of years to create the reef structure. Coral reefs provide shelter and food for thousands of fish and sea creature species. Many medicines used to treat human diseases have been developed from chemicals found in reef organisms.' The central idea is 'Coral reefs form over time and support both wildlife and human health.' Which detail from the passage does NOT support this central idea?
choices: Coral polyps build hard outer skeletons that stack on top of each other over hundreds of years.
Coral reefs provide shelter and food for thousands of fish and sea creature species.
Many medicines used to treat human diseases come from chemicals found in reef organisms.
Polyps are tiny animals that make up the structure of coral reefs.
hints: Ask yourself: does this detail explain why the reef forms, why it lasts long, or what lives there and benefits from it?
The central idea is about the reef's structure and what depends on it—not about medicines, even though the passage mentions them.

problemText: Read this passage: 'Jellyfish have existed in Earth's oceans for over 500 million years, making them older than dinosaurs. They survive in nearly every ocean environment, from warm tropical waters to the freezing Arctic. Jellyfish have no brain, no heart, and no blood, yet they can still hunt prey using stinging tentacles and digest food in a simple stomach pouch. Their simple body structure allows them to thrive with minimal energy and resources.' A student claims the central idea is 'Jellyfish have been on Earth longer than dinosaurs.' Is this claim correct? Why or why not?
choices: Yes, this is correct because the passage states jellyfish existed over 500 million years ago.
No, this is not correct because this statement is only one detail from the text and does not account for what the whole passage keeps returning to across multiple sentences.
Yes, this is correct because it is the most interesting fact in the passage.
No, this is not correct because the passage does not mention dinosaurs in the second or third sentence.
hints: Apply the two-detail test from the lesson: can you find two separate places in the passage that support 'Jellyfish have been on Earth longer than dinosaurs'?
Notice what idea the passage keeps coming back to—not just when they arrived, but how they survive with their simple body design, where they live, and how they hunt.

problemText: Read this passage: 'Penguins are flightless birds that live almost entirely in the Southern Hemisphere, with most species living near Antarctica. Their wings have evolved into flippers that make them excellent swimmers rather than fliers. A penguin's dense feathers and a thick layer of blubber underneath keep it warm in water temperatures near freezing. The shape of a penguin's body is streamlined, which reduces water resistance and helps it move quickly while hunting for fish.' A student writes two possible central ideas: (1) 'Penguins have adapted to survive in extremely cold ocean environments.' (2) 'Penguins live only in Antarctica and cannot fly.' Which central idea is better supported by the full passage, and why?
choices: Neither central idea works because the passage contains facts about both adaptation and habitat.

Idea 1 is better because it connects the passage's repeated focus on physical features (flippers, feathers, blubber, streamlined body) that all work together to let penguins thrive in cold water, whereas Idea 2 only names one detail about location.
Idea 2 is better because it correctly states that penguins cannot fly, which is the most important fact.
Both central ideas are equally good because they are both stated directly in the passage.
hints: Return to the lesson rule: a central idea must be broad enough to cover every paragraph or every major point in the text, not narrow enough to fit only one detail.

Look at how many details support Idea 1 (flippers for swimming, dense feathers, blubber layer, streamlined body) and how many support Idea 2 (the passage does name Antarctic habitat, but what else connects to that location fact?).

problemText: Read this passage: 'Porcupines are covered with roughly 30,000 sharp quills that act as their primary defense. Unlike hedgehogs, porcupine quills have tiny barbs at the tip that make them difficult to remove once they stick into skin. The quills are coated with an oil that prevents infection if they pierce an animal's body. When threatened, a porcupine does not shoot its quills; instead, it backs into its attacker or curls into a tight ball with its quills pointing outward.' A student writes the central idea: 'Porcupine quills are the porcupine's only survival tool.' Is this central idea correct? Using the lesson's two-detail test, explain whether you can find two separate supporting details from the passage that prove this statement is true, or whether the passage contradicts it.
choices: Yes, the central idea is correct because the passage clearly states that quills are the 'primary defense' and repeatedly discusses different aspects of how the quills function to protect the porcupine from harm.

No, the central idea is not correct because while the passage does explain how quills work as a defense (barbs make them stick, oil prevents infection, and the porcupine's behavior backs the defense), these details show quills work alongside the porcupine's own actions like backing into attackers or curling into a ball, not as the only tool.

Yes, the central idea is correct because the passage provides multiple details about quill structure, including the barbs at the tip and the protective oil coating that work together to make them effective.
No, the central idea is not correct because the passage does not specify the exact number of different types of quills or explain whether all quills have barbs and oil coating in equal amounts.
hints: The lesson teaches that a detail supporting a central idea must connect back to that idea. Ask: does the passage show the porcupine's own movements and behaviors also playing a role in its survival, not just the quills alone?

Look for a detail that shows the porcupine doing something actively (not just being a quill-covered animal) to survive. What does the porcupine do when threatened that works with—not instead of—its quills?

problemText: Which of these is the first step when you begin writing an objective summary of an informational text?
choices: Look through the passage to find all the interesting facts and list them in order.
Start by writing down the central idea of the text, which you have already identified.
Add your own thoughts about what the passage teaches and why it matters.
Recount every sentence from the passage in the same order the passage uses.
hints: The lesson says the central idea 'becomes the first sentence of the summary.'
Finding the central idea was done in a previous lesson, so you are not hunting for it again here.

problemText: A passage explains that many plants need sunlight, water, and soil to grow. The central idea is that plants require three things: sunlight, water, and soil. Which sentence should you leave out of your summary? A) Plants need sunlight to make food. B) Plants need water for their roots to absorb nutrients. C) Plants need soil to stay anchored in place. D) Plants with colorful flowers look beautiful in gardens.
choices: Sentence A, because it mentions only one of the three things plants need.
Sentence B, because it adds extra detail about how water works.
Sentence C, because it explains why soil matters to a plant.
Sentence D, because it does not explain why plants need the three things to grow.
hints: A summary keeps only details that connect back to the central idea.
The central idea is about what plants need to grow, not about what keeps them standing upright.

problemText: Read this student summary: 'Hurricanes form over warm ocean water where the air is moist. The warm water makes the air rise, and as it rises, it cools and forms clouds. The spinning motion of Earth causes the clouds to spin faster and faster. Eventually, the storm becomes so powerful that it destroys buildings and causes terrible damage.' The central idea is that hurricanes form and grow stronger over warm water because of rising air and spinning motion. What is the main problem with this summary?
choices: It leaves out important details about when hurricanes happen during the year.
It includes a sentence that gives the summarizer's own judgment instead of reporting what the passage says.
It is too short and does not explain enough about how hurricanes form.
It retells every fact from the passage instead of picking out only the supporting details.
hints: Look at how many separate sentences the summary has and whether each one is a key fact or a smaller detail.
A summary should be noticeably shorter than the passage because not every fact matters equally.

problemText: A passage explains: 'Bees carry pollen from flower to flower as they collect nectar. When a bee lands on a flower, pollen sticks to its fuzzy body. As the bee moves to the next flower, some of that pollen rubs off on the new flower's center. This cross-pollination helps the flower make seeds. Some flowers have bright colors and sweet smells to attract bees.' The central idea is that bees help flowers make seeds by carrying pollen from one flower to another. Which of these would be the best objective summary?
choices: Bees help flowers make seeds by carrying pollen from one flower to another as they collect nectar; pollen sticks to their fuzzy bodies and rubs off onto the next flower's center.

Bees visit flowers to drink nectar and carry pollen. Pollen sticks to their fuzzy bodies. Then the pollen rubs off on new flowers. Flowers have bright colors and sweet smells. This helps flowers make seeds.
Bees are amazing helpers for flowers because they carry pollen without even thinking about it, which shows how perfect nature is.
Bees collect nectar from flowers. When they land, pollen sticks to them. Bees then fly to another flower. The pollen rubs off. This makes seeds.
hints: A good summary combines related details into one or two clear sentences instead of listing each fact as its own short sentence.
Watch out for judgments like 'amazing' or 'perfect,' and remember that every sentence should connect directly to the central idea.

problemText: A passage says: 'Mirrors reflect light back to your eyes, which is why you see your own image when you look at one. A flat mirror reflects light at the same angle it receives it, so the image you see is the same size as you are. A curved mirror can bend light more or less, which is why mirrors in fun houses make you look stretched or squished.' The central idea is that you see your image in a mirror because light bounces back to your eyes at a specific angle. A student wrote this summary: 'Mirrors show you your image because light bounces back at the same angle it hits the mirror. Curved mirrors are weird because they bend light differently and make people look silly.' Which problem does this summary have?
choices: It includes a quiet judgment when it says curved mirrors are 'weird' and make people look 'silly,' reporting the summarizer's opinion instead of a fact.
It fails to mention that flat mirrors keep your image the same size as you are.
It does not explain clearly enough how light bounces inside a mirror.
It adds a detail about fun houses that was not part of the central idea.
hints: Two students who disagree about whether mirrors are interesting should still be able to sign the same summary.
Compare the student's summary to the central idea and ask what information the central idea requires that the summary leaves out.

problemText: A passage explains how salt helps keep ice cream from melting as fast as regular ice: 'When you freeze ice cream without salt, the ice stays at 32 degrees Fahrenheit, which is its normal freezing point. Salt lowers the freezing point of ice, making the ice much colder, sometimes down to 5 degrees or below. The colder the ice is, the longer it takes for the ice cream to melt. At very cold temperatures, the heat from the ice cream container cannot warm the ice fast enough to make it melt into liquid water.' The central idea is that salt keeps ice cream from melting quickly because salt makes ice colder than it normally would be, and colder ice melts more slowly. A student is deciding between two summaries. Summary 1: 'Salt lowers the freezing point of ice, making it much colder than regular ice. The ice cream stays frozen longer in very cold ice because the heat from the container cannot warm it fast enough to melt.' Summary 2: 'Without salt, ice stays at 32 degrees, but salt makes it go down to 5 degrees or below. The colder ice melts slower. Heat from the ice cream container cannot warm the ice fast enough.' Which summary better follows the rules for an objective summary, and why?
choices: Summary 2 is better because it includes all the temperatures mentioned in the passage.
Summary 1 is better because it connects each detail directly to why salt works, and combines related ideas into fewer, fuller sentences.
Both summaries are equal because they both report facts from the passage without adding judgment.
Summary 2 is better because it repeats the passage's own words instead of combining ideas.
hints: A summary should be noticeably shorter than the passage by picking out only what supports the central idea, not by including every number or detail the passage gives.
Think about how many separate facts Summary 1 ties together in one sentence versus how many short, separate sentences Summary 2 uses for the same facts.

problemText: A marine biologist examines the symbiosis, the close relationship between two organisms where each one benefits from the other, that exists between clownfish and sea anemones. Which meaning of symbiosis comes directly from the passage?
choices: A shared living space in which many different sea creatures occupy the same reef area and compete for resources.
A harmful relationship in which one organism hunts, captures, and consumes another organism for food.
A close relationship between two organisms where each one benefits from the other.
A short-term partnership that forms only during specific times of the year when organisms need to breed.
hints: Look for the exact phrase the passage uses right after the comma to define the term.
Do not add any information beyond what the passage actually states after the dash or comma.

problemText: A chef explains that tempering chocolate, the slow process of heating and cooling chocolate to precise temperatures so it sets with a smooth, shiny finish, requires patience and attention. If you swap the meaning from the passage back into the sentence, which phrase should make sense in place of the underlined term?
choices: Making chocolate taste better by adding extra cocoa butter.
Mixing chocolate with other ingredients to change its flavor.
The slow process of heating and cooling chocolate to precise temperatures so it sets with a smooth, shiny finish.
Keeping chocolate at room temperature for several hours before use.
hints: Use the swap-back test: which meaning fits smoothly where the technical term was used?
Eliminate choices that add information not printed in the passage itself.

problemText: An entomologist studies the metamorphosis of butterflies, describing stages such as caterpillar, chrysalis, and adult butterfly, to understand how insects change shape completely during their life cycle. Based on the examples the passage provides, what does metamorphosis mean in this context?
choices: A complete change in body shape and form that an insect goes through during its life cycle.
The process of growing larger and developing wings on an insect's body.
A period of time when an insect rests and does not move or eat.
The ability of certain insects to produce light or change colors when threatened.
hints: Look for example clues introduced by words such as 'such as' that show what the term covers.
Notice which choice matches the specific examples of caterpillar, chrysalis, and adult butterfly the passage lists.

problemText: A student reads: 'The astronomer measures the luminosity, the total amount of light energy a star gives off, of distant stars to compare how bright they really are, not how bright they seem from Earth.' The student first thinks luminosity means 'how bright something looks to your eye.' Why is that everyday meaning a trap here, and what should the student do instead?
choices: The everyday meaning confuses luminosity with apparent brightness, which is only what we see from Earth rather than the star's actual total light output; the student should apply the restatement that follows the comma to learn the real meaning.

The everyday meaning leaves out the crucial detail that luminosity is the total light energy the star actually gives off, not just how bright it appears from Earth; the student should use the restatement the passage provides after the comma.

The everyday meaning fails to account for the distance between Earth and the star, so it cannot measure how much total energy the star produces in space; the student should trust the passage's explanation instead of relying on visual impression.

The everyday meaning focuses on human perception rather than on the measurable, actual amount of light a star emits into space; the student should replace it with the technical definition the passage supplies right after the comma.
hints: Identify the signal (comma or dash) that the text uses to hand you the correct meaning right away.
Remember that a multiple-meaning word carries one everyday sense that is exactly what gets in the way—trust the text's restatement, not what you knew before.

problemText: Two passages use the word reservoir in different fields. Passage 1 (geology): 'Geologists study the reservoir, the natural or artificial hollow in the ground that holds water or oil for long periods.' Passage 2 (medicine): 'A disease reservoir, such as birds or bats, is an animal population that carries a pathogen and can spread it to other species.' Why is it important to use the text's own clues in each passage, rather than using the same meaning for both?
choices: Technical words in geology always have longer definitions than words in medicine, so you need to count the words to know which definition is right.

The word 'reservoir' has a different, more exact meaning in each field, and each passage supplies its own restatement or example to show what it means inside that specific text; using the same everyday meaning for both would give you wrong answers in one or both cases.
Passages about animals use simpler words than passages about rocks, so the animal passage definition must be wrong.
The first passage gives a restatement but the second gives an example, so you should only trust the first passage and ignore the second one.
hints: Think about what the lesson taught: a domain word belongs to one field and the text supplies the meaning for that field.
Consider what happens when you swap each passage's meaning back into its own sentence: does it make sense in both cases?

problemText: A student encounters this passage: 'The geologist describes the escarpment, a long, steep slope of rock face created by erosion or faulting, and notes that hikers often mistakenly believe it is simply a very steep mountain.' The student has never heard the word escarpment before and does not know what 'erosion' or 'faulting' mean either. Using only the clues the passage supplies, what is the best strategy to determine what escarpment means without needing to look up those two unfamiliar terms?
choices: Ignore the definition after the comma because you do not understand all the words in it, and instead search through the rest of the passage for sentences that might contain simpler descriptions or helpful examples.
Stop and look up both 'erosion' and 'faulting' in a reference source before you read any further, then return to reread the restatement once you understand those terms fully.

Use the comparison the passage makes between an escarpment and a steep mountain to infer that they must be almost identical, and decide that escarpment is just another word for mountain, even though the passage says hikers are mistaken about this.

Ask yourself what the overall topic of the sentence is (comparing what an escarpment really is to what hikers mistakenly think it is), use the restatement the passage supplies right after the comma, and notice that even if some words in the restatement are new, the core meaning is 'a long, steep slope of rock face,' which you can understand and swap back into the sentence to confirm it makes sense.
hints: The lesson teaches that you do not need to already know every single word the text uses—your job is to find the clues the text provides close by.
Remember the swap-back test: you can confirm your meaning even when part of the restatement holds unfamiliar terms, as long as you can grasp the core phrase and verify it fits the sentence.

problemText: A text feature is any part of a section added on purpose to help readers. Which of the following is a text feature? A photograph showing a volcano. A caption under the photograph. A sentence in the main paragraph. An empty space on the page.
choices: A photograph showing a volcano
A caption under the photograph
A sentence in the main paragraph
An empty space on the page
hints: Remember: a text feature is something a writer adds ON PURPOSE to help understanding—not the main paragraph sentences themselves.
Which choice is something the writer deliberately chose to include as a tool to help readers?

problemText: A history textbook section about the Civil War has three headings: 'The War Begins', 'Major Battles', and 'The War Ends'. A student wants to find information about the Battle of Gettysburg. Which heading should the student read first to locate that information? Which of the following best explains what that heading accomplishes for the reader?
choices: It tells the reader which section to read—'Major Battles'—so the reader can find Gettysburg without reading about when the war started or how it ended
It organizes the textbook by historical time periods so that readers know battles only happened during the middle section of the war
It summarizes the most important facts about the Battle of Gettysburg and explains why it changed the course of the Civil War
It provides information about the generals and soldiers who participated in the Battle of Gettysburg and their strategies
hints: A heading names the TOPIC of a section and separates it from other sections. Does it tell you the answer to your question, or does it tell you WHERE to find the answer?
Think about what a heading does NOT do: it doesn't give you all the details about a topic, it just names what that section covers.

problemText: An article about penguins includes a paragraph that says: 'Penguins are flightless birds that live in very cold climates. Most species live in the Southern Hemisphere, where temperatures stay below freezing for much of the year.' Below the paragraph is a map showing the coastlines where different penguin species live. What does the map contribute to the reader's understanding that the paragraph alone does not clearly provide?
choices: The precise degrees of temperature recorded in each location where penguins have been observed throughout the entire year
The specific locations and boundaries of where different penguin species are actually found on Earth
The historical dates when each penguin species first arrived in the locations where they currently live today
The detailed description of how penguins adapted their bodies and behaviors to survive in cold ocean environments
hints: Use the thumb test: cover the map and reread the paragraph. What information about penguin locations is missing from the paragraph?
A graphic shows relationships and locations that would take many sentences to describe. What can you see all at once on the map that the paragraph could not show?

problemText: A science article about how plants grow includes a labeled diagram showing the parts of a seed—the root, stem, and leaves—and how each grows in a different direction underground or above ground. The paragraph beside the diagram says: 'When a seed sprouts, the root grows downward into the soil to collect water and nutrients, while the stem pushes upward through the soil and the leaves unfold to catch sunlight.' The same article includes a sidebar that reads: 'Did you know? Some seeds can stay dormant in soil for years before sprouting.' Why is the diagram a better choice for showing how seed parts grow in different directions than the sidebar would be?
choices: The sidebar provides general background knowledge, but the diagram shows the exact spatial relationships all at once, which the paragraph's sentence-by-sentence description would take longer to make clear
The sidebar tells a reader something new, but the diagram repeats what the paragraph already said
The diagram saves space on the page, while the sidebar takes up too much room
The sidebar is only for fun facts, while the diagram is for serious information
hints: Think about what each text feature does: a diagram shows relationships and position all in one glance, while a sidebar adds a separate, related fact without interrupting the main explanation.
Ask yourself: which feature directly supports the main paragraph's explanation of how seed parts grow, and which one stands apart as an extra detail?

problemText: An article about ancient Egypt includes a section titled 'How Egyptians Built the Pyramids'. The paragraph under that heading explains the step-by-step process: workers cut stone blocks, transported them using ramps and sleds, and stacked them in precise rows. Below the paragraph is a photograph of the interior of a pyramid, showing narrow stone passages and chambers. The caption reads: 'The inside of a pyramid, showing the passages and chamber built into the massive structure.' A student reads only the paragraph and the heading, then skips the photograph and caption. What is the student missing that the caption provides?
choices: An explanation of why the Egyptians built pyramids in the first place
The names of all the workers and builders involved in pyramid construction
A visual understanding of how the interior of a pyramid is actually organized—the passages and chambers that the paragraph's word description alone does not make concrete
Proof that the paragraph's description of the pyramid-building process is completely accurate in every detail
hints: Use the thumb test: what does the photograph and caption show you that the paragraph's sentences do not already make clear to you?
A caption adds something the picture and paragraph do NOT already give. It might show a detail visually that was only described in words, or it might add brand-new information.

problemText: A magazine article about weather patterns includes a section with the heading 'How Hurricanes Form'. The paragraph explains that warm ocean water, low pressure, and wind patterns work together to create rotating storms. Next to the paragraph is a four-step labeled diagram showing the progression of a hurricane from a tropical disturbance to a full hurricane, with arrows showing wind movement at each stage. Below the diagram is a caption: 'The stages of hurricane development, showing how wind patterns change as the storm strengthens.' In the same section, there is also a sidebar stating: 'The costliest hurricane in U.S. history was Hurricane Katrina in 2005.' A reader covers the diagram with their thumb, rereads the main paragraph, and then uncovers the diagram. What has the diagram contributed to this section that the paragraph cannot do equally well?
choices: It shows in one glance how the four stages of hurricane development follow a sequence and how wind patterns transform visibly from one stage to the next, which the paragraph's description of conditions does not make as easy to hold in your mind at once
It demonstrates that Hurricane Katrina was the most destructive storm because it followed the exact pattern shown in the diagram's four stages
It explains which warm ocean waters and low pressure systems are necessary to begin the hurricane formation process from the very first stage
It identifies the specific dates and times when hurricanes are most likely to form during the Atlantic storm season
hints: Ask: what does a graphic show about relationships and sequences that would need many sentences to describe step by step?
The thumb test: if you read only the paragraph, do you understand the sequence and transformation of wind patterns as clearly as if you saw it all mapped out visually?
